liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Dark Star ran in a continuous segue chain through St. Stephen, The Eleven and Lovelight; Dark Star is rated among the best of 1969 and flows into a standout St. Stephen [1][10][12]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review, 1 other source): Morning Dew was played as the encore; Morning Dew builds to a striking crescendo at its end [1][10]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Pigpen is singled out as being at his finest on Lovelight [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-02-21.sbd.miller.111780.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 103 min; rated 4.36/5 by 14 [1]
- **gd69-02-21.sbd.owen.7859.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 105 min; rated 3.64/5 by 22 [2]. Said about its sound: The source tape ran slow, so it was sped up 4% and given a light noise filter to reduce hiss; A faint high-frequency whine is audible, noticeable during Morning Dew but present across the whole recording [2][4]

## Around the show

- The set is much shorter than the other Dream Bowl show, but is played slightly better [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-02-21.sbd.miller.111780.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [1]
- **gd69-02-21.sbd.owen.7859.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by The Wizard; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Edited and mastered for CD by The Wizard; no cassette flips suggest the source avoided a cassette generation; The tape may still be a further reel generation, with an off-speed recorder somewhere in its history; The tape circulated in the 1990s alongside the April Avalon shows and the August Aqua Theatre show [2][3]
